books.title: Infrastructure as Code: Designing and Delivering Dynamic Systems for the Cloud Age
books.access: Official 26-page excerpt; complete Chapter 1. Author, publisher, full-text and library searches did not establish a complete open third edition. Subscription or eligible library access may supply the rest.
read_sections: Chapter 1, What Is Infrastructure as Code?, complete printed pages 1–18
Chapters 19 and 20: public introductory previews only; complete contents inspected

findings.failure: Large untested changes entangle unrelated resources.
findings.mechanism: Use small versioned components and test each change.
findings.conditions: Choose boundaries around actual workload needs.
findings.counterexample: A single configuration repository does not guarantee independent deployment.
findings.verification: Inspect the affected resource set and run a disposable change-and-recovery exercise.

limitations: Chapter 1 supplies principles, not detailed Terraform execution guarantees. Detailed delivery chapters were not read in full.
Current Terraform plan, locking, lifecycle, and partial-apply documentation supplies operational constraints.

books.access: Publisher sample and author-hosted Chapter 3; public pattern summaries. Full-book searches found subscription/library routes, not an authenticated open complete edition. Published 2003, copyright 2004.
read_sections: Complete Chapter 2, Integration Styles, printed pages 39–56
Complete Message Endpoint pattern, printed pages 95–97, in Chapter 3
Abbreviated public Idempotent Receiver, Transactional Client, Message Expiration, and Guaranteed Delivery entries
Introduction: explicit limitations of illustrative code

findings.failure: Transport decisions leak into domain behavior.
findings.mechanism: Select integration style deliberately; isolate transport mapping in an endpoint.
findings.conditions: Retain observable delivery and failure semantics.
findings.counterexample: An endpoint wrapper cannot erase broker-specific guarantees.
findings.verification: Test application behavior independently, then test its real transport boundary.

limitations: Do not claim the public pattern summaries are complete book patterns.
Historical illustrative code omits production concerns; no code was imported.

Chapter 11, Consistency and Concurrency in Event-Driven Systems, complete printed pages 101–110

findings.failure: A successful live migration hides broken historical replay.
findings.mechanism: Define retained history, ownership, transaction and schema boundaries.
findings.conditions: Replay duration and older reader/writer combinations remain feasible.
findings.counterexample: A Kafka transaction does not cover an external payment.
findings.verification: Crash at effect/offset boundaries; replay old schemas into a new projection.

limitations: 2018 broker defaults and consumer-group limitations are historical.
Book schema generalizations require current format-specific checks; registry existence does not establish payload validation.
Complete source access does not mean every chapter was read.

books.title: Site Reliability Engineering
books.access: Official complete HTML book. This pass re-read selected Chapter 26 sections, extending existing repository reading notes.
read_sections: Chapter 26: Knowing That Data Recovery Will Work
Prior reading scope retained in docs/research/sre-reliability-reading.md

findings.failure: Stored backup files cannot restore usable service.
findings.mechanism: Rehearse restoration and validate application invariants.
findings.counterexample: A checksum success says nothing about restored user access.
findings.verification: Measure recovery time and restored data loss against objectives.

limitations: Google case studies motivate design; they do not specify another platform’s runtime contract.
No new claim of complete-book reading.

books.title: The Site Reliability Workbook
books.access: Official complete HTML book; selected Chapter 16 section re-read.

findings.trigger: Deploying changes to long-running pipeline workers.
findings.failure: A short health check misses work-unit failures.
findings.mechanism: Observe complete work units with stable canary/control attribution.
findings.counterexample: Pod readiness alone is not job-completion evidence.
findings.verification: Run a representative unit through the deployment and compare outcomes.

limitations: Accelerated interruption tests do not replace representative-duration validation.

books.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
books.access: Reuse of earlier user-supplied, commit-pinned draft reading; no newly asserted final-edition or full-book reading.
read_sections: Prior selected Chapters 11–13 processing/recovery sections documented in docs/research/ddia-processing-recovery.md

findings.failure: Mutable inputs change the recovered result.
findings.mechanism: Preserve input identity and required processing context.
findings.conditions: History and dependencies survive the replay horizon.
findings.counterexample: Rereading a current lookup table is not historical replay.
findings.verification: Change live inputs after checkpointing, then verify the declared recovery result.

limitations: Mirror identifies early-release material; final publication equivalence is not established.
Current platform contracts govern implementation details.

books.title: Release It! Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software
books.access: Reuse of earlier reading from an institutional complete-looking PDF; internal edition matched publisher metadata, but publisher authentication was not established.
read_sections: Previously read complete Chapters 5, 13, and 14; details in docs/research/full-text-access-operations.md

findings.trigger: Changing services while older work remains active.
findings.mechanism: Preserve compatibility through the overlap period.
findings.conditions: Track the final old consumer or job.
findings.counterexample: A completed pod rollout need not retire every old workflow.
findings.verification: Exercise old/new readers and writers before permitting contraction.

limitations: No new full-book reading in this pass.
Deployment guidance alone does not supply a durable handoff protocol.
